source_user: Calculation case 222: a model has 32 layers, 4 KV heads, head dimension 128, sequence length 3072, and BF16/FP16 KV values. Estimate bytes for one request's K/V cache. Show the formula and report GiB.
source_assistant: Use 2 × layers × sequence_length × KV_heads × head_dim × bytes_per_value. Here this is 2 × 32 × 3072 × 4 × 128 × 2 = 201326592 bytes = 0.187500 GiB. This excludes allocator metadata and other runtime memory.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions (falsifiable; check each against the model config.json and the serving engine's KV dtype flag before trusting the number): standard MHA/GQA attention with exactly one K tensor and one V tensor per layer; 4 KV heads (under GQA/MQA the KV footprint scales with KV heads, never with query heads); head_dim 128; a single request holding its full 3072-token context; KV dtype BF16/FP16 (2 B/value); 1 GiB = 2^30 B; no prefix sharing, no cross-request block reuse, no KV offload.

Formula: bytes = 2 (K and V) x layers x seq_len x kv_heads x head_dim x bytes_per_value.
Substituting: 2 x 32 x 3072 x 4 x 128 x 2 = 201326592 B = 0.187500 GiB (192.000 MiB).
Derived rate: 65536 B per token per request (64.000 KiB/token). The per-token rate, not the single-request total, is the number to use when sizing max_num_seqs x max_model_len against free HBM.

Mechanism: each decode step appends one K and one V vector of size kv_heads x head_dim in every one of the 32 layers, so KV bytes grow linearly in generated tokens and linearly in concurrency. Weights are a fixed cost; KV is the elastic one, so on a fixed HBM budget KV is what caps batch size and therefore throughput. When the KV pool is exhausted a paged engine preempts and recomputes rather than OOMing, which shows up as a throughput cliff plus TTFT/ITL tail spikes rather than a crash - so a rising preemption counter, not a memory error, is the signal to watch.

KV is stored at 16-bit here. Switching to FP8/INT8 KV would halve this to 100663296 B, but that is a lossy change: gate it on a long-context accuracy A/B against a BF16-KV control before claiming the capacity win.

Boundary conditions this estimate does NOT cover, all of which push the real footprint up: (1) PagedAttention block padding - at block_size 16 a 3072-token request occupies 192 blocks and the final partial block is wasted; (2) the KV pool is preallocated, so gpu_memory_utilization reserves it up front and per-request free HBM will not visibly move; (3) attention/workspace scratch, CUDA graph capture pools, activation buffers and NCCL communication buffers sit outside this formula; (4) under tensor parallelism of degree TP the KV heads are sharded, so per-GPU KV is roughly this figure / TP only while TP <= kv_heads (4) - beyond that KV heads must be replicated and per-GPU KV stops shrinking; (5) speculative decoding, beam search and multi-sample requests multiply the live KV per logical request.

Evidence required before acting on this: the config.json values for num_hidden_layers, num_key_value_heads and head_dim; the engine's reported KV cache dtype and the number of KV blocks it allocated at startup; and a measured HBM curve from nvidia-smi or torch.cuda.memory_allocated at a known concurrency, compared against this analytic figure. Treat this as an estimate (a lower bound on real usage), not a measurement.

Rollback gate: if measured steady-state KV usage exceeds this analytic value by more than ~15%, or preemption count per minute rises above zero at the target concurrency, reduce max_model_len or max_num_seqs and revert any KV-dtype or block-size change before continuing to raise load.
